answer: The guild issues each applicant a sealed sable-bound notebook and a tagged plot on the east vine wall. For five dawns the applicant writes one quatrain in the notebook—completing a sonnet on the last dawn—while a duty clerk photographs the open page beside the tagged internode, which must have grown 8 mm since day one. The clerk stamps a one-time carbon receipt. Two notebooks sharing a fiber UV barcode, or photographs sharing a camera-body serial, forfeit both 70-unit deposits, and the issuing clerk is suspended for 28 days. Each plot graduates only one agent every 18 days.
